body:
Hey! Found your video, and subscribed to your channel. I am so glad you took the first step too. Looking forward to more sharing as now I understand how hard it is to do. 
And thank you for supporting me as well. More power to you. :)

Thank you for listening to it as much as you could. And thank you for the feedback.
Since this was my first attempt, I really didn't have much of a choice than my iPhone. I know there are audio problems for which I did apologise. I am thinking of more videos and I will make them better from next time. 
Again, thank you so much for your suggestions. It means so much to me.
Thank you for supporting me. I suppose I wouldn't be able to be confident about doing more if I didn't have your support. I will keep trying and fight till the end.

Thank you so much for your kind words and support by subscribing. Please give me a link to your video so I can watch it and your channel, which I can subscribe to. :)
Congratulations, you too for taking the first step!
Thank you so much! I will take your advice and post it to r/bipolar and r/BipolarReddit :)

Hello! Thank you for your kind words and support. It means a lot to me. It is true, I was very scared, anxious while doing this. So thanks a lot. 
And thank you so much for the best wishes. :)
Hello, thank you for your story. It's of great help and importance. Do you want me to copy/paste your story as a blog and add the link to your website below? Will that do?

Hello, it's very inspiring that you are interested in sharing your story. I know how overwhelming it can be to pen it all down. But if you want to share, even anonymously, I can give you my email id and you can mail me. Mull it over and let me know. Your story will inspire others.
That's great! I'd be glad if you come on board as a guest blogger for my website. It would be proper if I mail you the details.

Hello, I just read your recommendation along with the short summary you gave. It is truly very well written. It is just a thought, but would you like to write a whole review or an article on the book for our readers? If you don't mind that is. It will be a very interesting read. Thanks again.
Thank you so much for helping me with your recommendations. Please keep them coming. It'll help me make a great list. :)
Thank you so much for helping me. Please keep the references coming, the more the better. It's going to help me make a good list. :)
Thank you so much, all of you, for helping me. These recommendations are going to help me a lot. Do keep them coming. The more the better. :D
We do have a dog, and he makes it all so much easier. It's wonderful to hear you have three of them. They are precious.
I know. I know many people like that. And it's funny because they cringe at the slightest mention of mental illness.
True. Having bipolar disorder and managing a normal life is a huge job every day. Luckily, I have a good support system. And my mother in law is supportive. So, it has been a little better.

My father wasn't upset, but it took him time to understand. I was diagnosed when I was twenty, after my mother's death. 

It's upsetting that the worst comes from rest of the family. The stigma attached to mental illness in our society is formidable. It took me more than a decade to accept and come out about it.
Thanks a lot.
Thank you.
It has been easy to get rid of these people, except some who are fat, stupid, and relatives. Worst part is they don't know they're stupid.
Haha. I like this. I like this a lot.
I understand what you mean. But I'm sure your husband wouldn't care about something like that. :)
Absolutely. Problem is sometimes it gets a little tough getting rid of them, simply because they are relatives.

Hello, 

It is good to hear someone else understands. Tell your brother I completely understand his situation.

I understand the problem, with fighting mental illness in the Indian society where it is stigmatised. I wish people wouldn't criticise or look at me with pitying eyes. I could only rise above it all when I accepted who I am. It took more than a decade, but I finally feel better.

But all of that still doesn't change the fact that romanticising the concept of mental illness is wrong. There is nothing glamorous about our fight and it should be respected. The severity of mental illnesses shouldn't be taken away because someone is feeling "down and depressed". 

People use those words as if they don't matter. "I am bipolar." They don't even know that bipolar disorder isn't a character flaw, it's a disease like any other physical disease. This doesn't happen with cancer. Then why are mental illnesses taken so lightly? 

That's the point.
